title: TensorTEE: Unifying Heterogeneous TEE Granularity for Efficient Secure Collaborative Tensor Computing
problem: Heterogeneous TEE designs for CPU-NPU collaborative computing suffer from mismatched memory granularities between CPU (cacheline-granularity) and NPU (cacheline-granularity MAC), intensifying memory pressure and storage constraints. Secure data transfer across heterogeneous enclaves requires unsafe transit through non-secure regions, incurring expensive re-encryption and complex scheduling overhead.
motivation: Heterogeneous CPU-NPU collaborative computing offers substantial performance benefits, but requires efficient secure execution mechanisms to protect data confidentiality and integrity during collaborative tensor computation.
method: TensorTEE proposes a unified memory granularity approach across heterogeneous CPU and NPU TEEs to reduce memory pressure from mismatched cacheline-based designs. The system streamlines secure data transfer across heterogeneous enclaves by eliminating the need for transit through non-secure regions, reducing re-encryption and scheduling overhead for collaborative tensor operations.
key_novelty: Unified memory granularity abstraction across heterogeneous CPU-NPU TEEs to eliminate inefficiencies in collaborative secure tensor computing.
contributions: Identifies memory granularity mismatches as a key bottleneck in heterogeneous TEE-based collaborative computing
Proposes TensorTEE architecture with unified TEE granularity for CPU-NPU systems
Addresses memory pressure and storage constraints from fine-grained cacheline designs
Streamlines secure data transfer across heterogeneous enclaves without transiting non-secure regions
primary_theme: Secure heterogeneous tensor computing with unified TEE granularity
